messages:
anya: Heads-up — long-chat repro on H100 shows steady GPU mem growth when paged KV is enabled. ~1.1GB growth per 1k tokens, no corresponding evict counter bumps in metrics.
jin: Tried same workload on RTX6000 and growth stabilizes. So looks arch-specific.
oliver: Can you paste the repro config? batch sizes, seq len, model, quantization?
anya: model: opt-6.7b (v2), seq=32768, gen step=1k (streaming convos), kv paging=on, page_size=64KB, allocator=slab-v2, kernel path=optimized/pagedattn. Batch-size varies due to streaming but avg concurrent requests ~12.
marcus: FWIW we've seen page table mismatch when page_size != GPU page alignment on H100 (huge page fallback interaction). Could be TLB flush mismatch.
anya: Adding logs — page table stats after 5k tokens: 
```
PTENTS total: 16384
active_pages: 14720
evicted_pages: 0
free_list.len: 964
page_ref.leak: 0x1e40
kv_cache_size_bytes: 12.3GB
```
Note evicted_pages stays zero the whole run.
kaitlyn: evicted_pages=0 and growth = suspicious. Any OOMs?
anya: No OOM, just steady increase until we hit reserved buffer then requests slow.
jin: Can you dump the page->slot mapping? The reproduction on RTX had non-zero evicts and we saw reuse. Maybe the PT entry widths differ.
anya: Pasted mapping snippet (truncated):
```
page_id: 0x3f7 -> slot 1024 (owner req 0x42)
page_id: 0x3f8 -> slot 1025 (owner req 0x43)
...
page_id: 0x4aa -> slot 1024 (owner req 0x89) // duplicate slot mapping
```
oliver: Duplicate slot -> that smells like a reuse race where freed slot is immediately reassigned but page table not updated atomically. On H100 kernel maybe the atomic CAS path falls back to a non-atomic due to 64-bit misalignment.
marcus: Also check kernel selection logs — if we fallback to the generic PagedAttention kernel for certain seq lengths we saw a codepath that does update page table in two ops (clear+set) instead of single atomic swap.
anya: Kernel selection log around the time: `chosen_kernel: paged_attn_opt_v2 (H100)`, but for some batches it printed `fallback_kernel: paged_attn_generic` with a note about unaligned strides.
kaitlyn: Unaligned strides — that matches H100's new mem-access rules for L2 caching. Could explain inconsistent ordering.
jin: Quick repro suggestion: run with `KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1 PAGER_TRACE=1 LD_PRELOAD=libpmemhook.so` and a tiny harness: 8 concurrent streams, long tail context, force page_size=64K. Capture `pager.trace`.
anya: I ran that and saw this interleaving (abbrev):
```
[thread-7] free_slot(slot=1024)
[thread-9] alloc_slot(slot=1024)
[thread-9] write_pt(page=0x4aa -> slot=1024)
[thread-7] clear_pt(page=0x4aa -> slot=1024)
```
So alloc/write races with clear. write_pt then clear_pt ordering causes PT to momentarily point to the new page but the old free still had a lingering ref (refcount not decremented in free fast-path).
oliver: That sequence explains duplicate mapping then growth because the stale physical backing isn't reclaimed — refcounts never hit zero.
marcus: Are refcounts per-page stored in host-mapped struct? On H100 kernel path we updated refcount in GPU kernel and deferred host sync. If host free assumes GPU refcount==0 immediately, can lose decreases.
kaitlyn: Proposed mitigation: add a small hazard window on free path (spin & check PT CAS result) or switch to atomic swap on both alloc/clear for H100. Might cost ~0.2ms but stops leak.
jin: Also add a metric for pt_cas_failures and stale_ref_detected so we can gauge incidence.
anya: Quick perf numbers: before change on long-run: 12k tokens/s overall, mem growth 1.1GB/1k tokens. With local patch (spin-waitCAS) I got stable memory and perf went to 11.7k tokens/s — small perf hit but acceptable for stability.
oliver: Can you open a small patch PR with guarded CAS path under feature flag `kv_pt_atomic_h100_fix`? We should gate by kernel/hw checks.
anya: Will do. Also adding regression test: stress_paged_kv.py which runs 16 streams, random seq lenses up to 64k, duration 10m, asserts evicted_pages > 0 and no mem growth > 50MB.
marcus: One more ask — run CUDA-MEMCHECK on fallback kernel; sometimes UVM semantics hide races. Also check syscalls around hugepage allocations.
kaitlyn: Filing follow-up: I'll coordinate with infra to get an H100 node in dedicated lab for 24h burn.
srebot: deploy-bot: canary rollout for `pagedattn_opt_v2` paused due to elevated pt_cas_fail rates reported by telemetry. :warning:
anya: Thanks — I'll send the patch + test in the next hour and reference this thread. If we need to revert canary, let's keep monitor alerts. :thumbsup:
jin: Nice debugging everyone. Let's land the CAS guard behind a flag and iterate on perf after.
